items.titleJp: 夜[よる]の静[しず]かな読書会[どくしょかい]
items.titleEn: Why a Bookstore Started Late-Night Silent Reading Events
items.situationEn: A radio host interviews the owner of an independent bookstore about a popular monthly event.

lines.en: Before, we held reading clubs where people shared impressions. However, regular customers told me they got nervous trying to say something clever in front of others, yet at home they end up checking their phones and can't focus on books.

lines.speaker: Owner
lines.jp: それで、発表[はっぴょう]のプレッシャーをなくして、ただスマホを置[お]いて読書[どくしょ]に没頭[ぼっとう]できる場[ば]を作[つく]ろうと思[おも]ったんです。
lines.en: So I decided to remove the pressure of speaking and create a space where people can simply put down their phones and immerse themselves in reading.

items.questionJp: 店長[てんちょう]はなぜこの読書会[どくしょかい]を始[はじ]めましたか。
items.questionEn: Why did the owner start this silent reading event?
choices: 夜[よる]の売上[うりあげ]を増[ふ]やすために閉店時間[へいてんじかん]を延[の]ばしたかったから
感想[かんそう]を言[い]う負担[ふたん]をなくし、集中[しゅうちゅう]して本[ほん]を読[よ]める場所[ばしょ]を作[つく]りたかったから
読書会[どくしょかい]の司会[しかい]をするスタッフがいなくなったから
参加者[さんかしゃ]同士[どうし]が静[しず]かにSNSで感想[かんそう]を投稿[とうこう]できるようにするため
choicesEn: To extend closing hours and increase nighttime sales
To remove the pressure of giving opinions and offer a distraction-free place to read
Because they ran out of staff to moderate discussions
So participants could quietly post reviews on social media
items.explanationEn: Customers felt stressed about presenting clever opinions and distracted by smartphones at home, so the owner created a pressure-free, focused reading space.

items.titleJp: 規格外[きかくがい]野菜[やさい]のレストラン
items.titleEn: A Chef's Mission with Imperfect Vegetables
items.situationEn: A chef speaks on a podcast about why her restaurant buys oddly shaped vegetables directly from farmers.

items.introEn: A chef is speaking on a podcast. What is the main point she wants to convey?

lines.en: Vegetables in supermarkets all have uniform shapes and sizes. Yet in reality, huge amounts of vegetables are discarded just for being slightly crooked or bruised, even though their flavor is identical.

lines.speaker: Chef
lines.jp: わたしの店[みせ]では、そういった野菜[やさい]を農家[のうか]さんから直接[ちょくせつ]買[か]い取[と]って、スープやカレーにしています。安[やす]く済[す]ませたいからではなく、見[み]た目[め]にこだわらなくても本当[ほんとう]においしい料理[りょうり]が作[つく]れることをお客[きゃく]さんに知[し]ってほしいんです。
lines.en: At my restaurant, we buy those vegetables directly from farmers and turn them into soups and curries. It's not to cut costs—I want customers to realize that truly delicious food can be made without obsessing over appearance.

lines.speaker: Chef
lines.jp: 食事[しょくじ]を楽[たの]しみながら、食品[しょくひん]ロスについて考[かんが]えるきっかけになればうれしいですね。

items.questionEn: What is the chef's main message?

見[み]た目[め]が不揃[ふぞろ]いでも味[あじ]は良[よ]く、おいしく食[た]べることで食品[しょくひん]ロスを意識[いしき]してほしい
農家[のうか]はもっと見[み]た目[め]のきれいな野菜[やさい]を育[そだ]てるべきだ
スーパーマーケットはスープやカレーの販売[はんばい]を始[はじ]めたほうがいい

Even oddly shaped vegetables taste great, and enjoying them can raise awareness of food waste
Supermarkets should start selling soup and curry
items.explanationEn: She explicitly states she does not use them just to save money, but to show that appearance doesn't affect taste and to inspire awareness about food waste.

keyPhrases.en: to become a trigger / opportunity for

items.titleJp: 同僚[どうりょう]からの急[きゅう]な頼[たの]み事[ごと]を断[ことわ]る
items.titleEn: Quick Response: Politely Declining an Urgent Favor at Work

items.introEn: A colleague asks for help at work, but you are too busy today. What is the most appropriate reply?

items.questionEn: How should you politely decline for today?
choices: ごめん、今[いま]ちょっと手[て]が離[はな]せなくて……。明日[あした]の朝[あさ]一番[いちばん]なら見[み]られるんだけど、それでも大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]？

Yeah, today is impossible, so I can't do anything.

keyPhrases.en: tied up / unable to take one's hands off current work

items.titleJp: スポーツジムの施設[しせつ]利用[りよう]案内[あんない]
